gappers.catalyst_detail: No Nebius-specific news. The move is the highest-beta expression of a market-wide AI rebound: Nasdaq-100 futures +2%, NVDA +4%, Marvell +7.3% on a fiscal-Q3 beat, with Deutsche Bank flagging that the tech selloff had 'stabilized'. The stock-specific facts still point the wrong way: Q3 (Nov 12) carried a LOWERED 2026 revenue outlook plus disclosed data-center delays, and 2027 guidance is $40-45B of capex against only $12-13B of revenue, funded largely by customer prepayments and asset-backed loans. A death cross (50-SMA under 200-SMA) formed in November; Citigroup kept Buy but cut its target from $324 to $265.
gappers.why: Leveraged sector beta. A capex-heavy, externally-funded buildout trades as a high-duration proxy on both AI sentiment and funding costs, so it falls hardest on margin warnings and bounces hardest on risk-on. No new Nebius information today.
gappers.impact: Reads as a one-day headline spike. The gap is only 0.37 ATR against an 18.6% ATR - barely a third of a normal session. Prior-session volume 40.81M vs 33.49M 20-day average is 1.22x: a tick up, but on a sector bounce day that is flow, not accumulation. Sector read-through is total - CRWV +5.59% in lockstep at rank 9, confirming beta over thesis. Price sits 49.2% below the 200-SMA with a confirmed death cross. The $40-45B/$12-13B capex-to-revenue structure is solvency-sensitive if AI credit tightens.

gappers.catalyst_detail: No Bloom Energy-specific news today; it is rising with the AI-power complex on the broad rebound. gappers.impact: Best fundamentals here, still not a tradeable setup. The gap is 0.51 ATR on a 13.1% ATR - half a normal day. Volume 18.67M vs an 18.04M 20-day average is 1.03x: no confirmation at all. Group move confirmed across fuel-cell peers. The stock has round-tripped 170.98 to 142.39 to 168.15 to 152.89 inside six sessions; in a 13%-ATR regime a 7% gap carries no information. At 26.8% below the 200-SMA this is the shallowest breach on the list - and still a fail.

A 1-ATR stop is 13.1% ($142.47, just below the Nov 20 low of $140.69), needing a +26% target near $207 for 2:1, which is reachable against the $230-335 analyst range, so the math works on paper. WATCH, trigger a reclaim of $224 (200-SMA) on above-average volume, then re-check Confluence via /trade.

Yet the stock set a new 52-week low ($8.24 intraday) in Nov 27 reporting and Roth cut its target from $30 to $20.
gappers.why: Sector beta, not news. The mechanism is the same multiple compression hitting the whole space group - record backlog and a revenue beat met by target cuts and a sliding share price. Today's move is the group re-rating off a 52-week low as risk appetite returns, not a re-pricing of Intuitive Machines.

FY26 revenue guidance has been raised three times this year - at least $125M, then $130M in May, $140M in August with a 28%+ gross-margin target, and $145M in the November release. Commercially it signed a multi-year supply agreement with Stark Future starting 2027 worth over $100M and took a $24.0M order from a major European drone developer. Analysts still cut: B.
